The module contains deliberately obfuscated, dynamically-evaluated code (eval/Function with an encoded payload) that runs during message processing (Indicator 1 and the large obfuscated block). That payload decodes and executes hidden logic, mutates global state and dynamically requires modules — behavior consistent with a hidden backdoor or data-exfiltration hook. The file also reads/writes local files (CountTime.json) and uses Facebook session cookies and websocket/mqtt connections to edge-chat.facebook.com (Indicators 2–11), giving it access to sensitive session data and live message streams. The combination of obfuscation + runtime eval + access to user cookies/message data is a clear malicious indicator.

Combined with impersonation/typosquatting indicators (fake RevenueCat metadata and unknown author), this is deliberate malicious data-exfiltration behavior.

This is intentional, malicious behavior (remote exfil/C2), not benign utility code.
